criteria.criterion: The trend section is absent (no line) when no class has enough landed jobs, so an empty history is not shown as success.

findings.summary: The new trend_section was inserted between repeated_causes_section and that function's doc comment, so the doc comment is now in the wrong place.
findings.evidence: Lines 902-903 ('The open repeated causes of Hestia's error review...') now sit directly above trend_section's own doc line. trend_section therefore carries two unrelated doc paragraphs, and repeated_causes_section has no doc comment. This goes against the 'strangers' default. Fix: move trend_section above that doc comment.

findings.summary: No test covers ClassTrend::compute, which joins job records (class_of_work) with landed_jobs; only the pure analyze() is tested.
findings.evidence: All four class_trend tests call analyze() on ClassedJob values they build directly. If the join between job ids and classes in compute broke, for example dropping every job, no test would fail; status would just stop printing the line. Fix: add a test that builds Records using the existing planning_cost_tests helpers.

findings.summary: Soundness: the job named as making things worse is simply the job of any class that landed just before the sustained rise; it does not show that job caused the rise. When the class has no sustained rise, the code instead names the job before the newer half.
findings.evidence: `before = positions[stays_from].saturating_sub(1)`, with `.unwrap_or(half)` as the fallback. This matches the accepted reading's design, and the measure text says 'after which', not 'caused by', so it is not misleading. Still, the fallback can name a job unrelated to any rise. A sounder alternative would report a culprit only when a sustained rise exists, or name the range of jobs between the last normal job and the first raised one.

findings.evidence: The diffstat shows 6 files, and hestia.rs is not among them. No change there was needed: the label check in status.rs passes. This is not a scope violation.

summary: The change passes. It gives requirement OLY-9-10 a working mechanism. A new module, crates/athena-core/src/class_trend.rs, sorts landed jobs by class of work. For each class with at least four landed jobs it compares the median minutes of the older half with the newer half. It reports which classes improved, and for a class that got worse it names the earlier landed job after which its cost rose. `athena status` prints this as a `trend` line and prints nothing while the history is too thin. docs/spec.toml now names this mechanism, keeps owner Hestia, and its measure ends with `status: trend`. I ran the targeted tests myself and they pass: the class_trend tests in athena-core, the measure-label test, the athena-cli rendering test and the xtask spec tests. fmt, clippy and the full test suite already passed in Athena's recorded checks. I found three minor problems and no blocking ones: (1) a doc comment in display.rs is in the wrong place; (2) no test covers how ClassTrend::compute reads real job records, only the pure analyze function; (3) naming the job that landed just before the rise as the cause is a rough guess, which the accepted design allows. hestia.rs was listed as a deliverable but was not changed, which was not needed.
